opportunities.gap: The 2FA framing stops at 'app-based 2FA' and treats SMS as implicitly equivalent. As of 2024-2026 the consensus has shifted: SMS codes are phishable (SIM-swap/relay), app TOTP codes are still phishable via real-time adversary-in-the-middle relay, and passkeys / FIDO2 are the phishing-resistant default offered by Google, Microsoft, and Apple. Critically, the section's own branching scenario has the attacker capture the password on a fake page; an app-based TOTP code typed into that same page would ALSO be captured, which the current text never acknowledges.
opportunities.proposed_change: Add a one-sentence ranking to the Core Concept 2FA row (or the Decision Rule second-factor check): not all second factors are equal. SMS is weakest (SIM-swap/relay); app TOTP codes are better but can still be relayed through a fake login page; passkeys / security keys are phishing-resistant because they are cryptographically bound to the real site's domain and cannot be entered on a lookalike page. Tie back to the branching-scenario 'breach' node: a passkey would have blocked the login even after the password (and even a TOTP code) was phished, because the lookalike domain cannot satisfy the WebAuthn origin check.
